messages:
Ken: FYI ACME hit us with a support escalation — streaming responses get cut mid-token when their clients run through a corporate HTTP proxy + our Dedicated private deployment behind a VPC. They see a couple 502/504s then a client reconnect that yields partial output. Can SRE/Runtime triage?

Jake (ACME): repro steps:
1) Start a streaming request (our SDK streaming=true) to the dedicated endpoint in their VPC.
2) Put a corp proxy between client and internet (Squid-like).
3) After ~12–25s the client sees a truncated final chunk, then a reconnect that returns the rest but with duplicated tokens and sometimes a 401 on reconnect.

Jake (ACME): sample curl I used: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://dedicated-acme.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-large"
```

Maria (sre): thanks. A few quick things we need: full proxy logs (connect/close), TCP captures from client side showing MSS/MTU, and the request/response headers (including any x-forwarded-* and keepalive).

Priya (eng-runtime): initial hunch: this smells like packet fragmentation / proxy buffer flush behavior. Corporate proxies sometimes buffer until a content-length or a flush threshold — with SSE/chunked streaming we depend on small flushes. If the proxy performs reassembly or rewrites TCP MSS, it can split SSE boundaries and the client lib may treat partial chunk as completed event.

Sam (onprem-eng): also verify if their VPC path-MTU-discovery is blocked (ICMP blackhole). If PMTU is broken, endpoints reduce MSS and we can end up with odd fragmentation boundaries across proxies; some proxies collapse small writes into larger frames which breaks streaming heuristics. On-prem ingress + corp proxy chain is particularly fragile.

Jake (ACME): attaching logs (redacted) — see proxy.log excerpt below (timestamps shortened):
```
[12:03:05] CONNECT client-ip -> proxy
[12:03:17] GET /v1/stream 200 chunked
[12:03:29] proxy flush 8192 bytes
[12:03:29] proxy conn reset -> 502
[12:03:31] CONNECT client-ip -> proxy (reused)
[12:03:31] GET /v1/stream 200 chunked (resume)
```

Jake (ACME): also noticed on reconnect the SDK sends the old session token; we rotate tokens every 20s in our client — sometimes the reconnect gets a 401.

Priya (eng-runtime): two distinct failure modes then: (A) proxy buffering/fragmentation causing SSE events to be split and interpreted as truncated; (B) reconnect auth tokens not preserved. For (A) we saw similar in an enterprise customer last year where setting explicit chunked transfer flushes on the app/proxy fixed it. Example server-side snippet we recommend to customers (node):
```
res.writeHead(200, {
  'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
  'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
  Connection: 'keep-alive'
});
res.write(':ok\n\n'); // initial ping
// on every token/event do res.write(`data: ${chunk}\n\n`) and then res.flush() if using compression/proxy
```

Priya (eng-runtime): also ask them to check their proxy for "buffer responses until X bytes" behavior. If present, tiny SSE frames get held until threshold, causing long pauses and then a large flush that the client mis-handles.

Maria (sre): for our side, please capture a tcpdump on the dedicated node for the failing session (client-ip -> nat -> dedicated) showing the sequence of FIN/RESET/packets around the moment of truncation. We want to see whether the connection is closed by our node, the proxy, or the client. Also include TLS version/ciphers from proxy logs if available.

Ken (support): note about auth: if the client rotates tokens on reconnect, we should make sure SDK exposes a reconnect hook to fetch a fresh token. Until then, we can advise the customer to use a long-lived session token for streaming or a token-refresh callback. Add to action items.

Sam (onprem-eng): quick workaround we pushed previously that might help immediately for Dedicated: reduce the TCP MSS on the egress NAT (linux sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 and/or adjust iptables MSS clamping) OR enable explicit chunked flush at ingress (nginx proxy: proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection "" to allow streaming). Example nginx conf snippet: 
```
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_pass https://backend;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
}
```

Jake (ACME): we asked infra to try proxy_buffering off and they said their corp proxy is managed and harder to change. They can do client-side tweaks though.

Priya (eng-runtime): we can implement a server-side defend: emit a periodic SSE comment/ping every 8–10s to keep proxy buffers from being idle. That reduces the chance of long-held frames. We'll schedule a short patch for Dedicated runtime to emit configurable heartbeat comments for private instances. Not a perfect fix but buys time.

Infra-bot: rollout scheduled: dedicated-runtime/heartbeat-ping v1.2 -> prod-dedicated-1 at 1950123600 (canary 10%).

Maria (sre): meanwhile action items:
- ACME to capture tcpdump + proxy logs and send to support (Jake).
- Ken to confirm whether reconnect 401s match their token rotation window or our gateway returns 401s after session close.
- Priya/Sam to add short-term heartbeat ping config to Dedicated runtime and produce a patch.
- SRE to monitor for increased reset/502 rates during canary rollout.

Ken (support): Jake — can you also tell us the client SDK name and version and whether you're using a custom reconnect policy? If you can reproduce with plain curl that helps isolate the proxy vs SDK behavior. Also include the Authorization header pattern (are you using ephemeral tokens per request or a session bearer?).

Jake (ACME): will do. I can repro with curl and will attach a tcpdump next update. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

Priya (eng-runtime): one more note on duplication: when clients reconnect we attempt to be idempotent by resending a small overlap of tokens (resume window) because we can't rely on exact byte offsets across proxies. If the client also replays some content we get doubled tokens. We should add a recommend config: on reconnect clients should request a resume offset from server (we'll add an opt-in header X-Resume-From in the next SDK versions).

Sam (onprem-eng): logging: set debug for streaming to capture "last-kv-id" we send in X-Stream-Resume in the response — that'll let us correlate duplicates in our logs.

Ken (support): capturing timeline. I'll mark this P1 for now due to customer impact on session continuity.

deploy-bot: completed canary deploy step for dedicated-runtime/heartbeat-ping v1.2 -> prod-dedicated-1/10% at 1950123625.

Maria (sre): good. We'll reconvene after Jake sends tcpdump and proxy logs. If anyone hits this in other customers, drop notes here (esp. corp-proxy + private Dedicated).

Ken (support): closing loop for now — leaving thread open for attachments.
